name: Samsung SDS Cloud Platform

modes.label: Virtual Server, no contract (hourly, open-source OS)
modes.note: Official USD list prices (USD/hour, "All prices exclude VAT", "Without Contract (USD/hour)") from the service portal price data (cloud.samsungsds.com/serviceportal/assets/js/data/price/virtualServerPrice.js, rendered at serviceportal/pricing.html?item=VS&product=compute), region KR_WEST (identical in KR_WEST_2), Open-source OS column. Sizes: 1st Gen (Ice Lake), 2nd Gen (Sapphire Rapids), 3rd Gen (Granite Rapids) standard Virtual Servers, 1-16 vCore. e.g. 4 vCore / 8 GB: $0.2191 (1st), $0.193 (2nd), $0.2052 (3rd). Billing unit/rounding not stated beyond "Charge by used hour"; granularity left null. "* 1 month (730 hours) is applied for usage without contract."

modes.label: Planned Compute 1 year
modes.note: Planned Compute 1-year (instance-type commitment), official USD list, KR_WEST (=KR_WEST_2), Open-source OS, VAT excluded. Fixed monthly fee per committed instance type; sizes.hour = monthly/730. Early cancellation penalty = monthly fee x 50% x remaining months. Discount vs on-demand is ~35% (1y) / ~40% (3y) for standard types, not the headline 'up to 55%'. Cost Savings (hourly spend commitment) gives near-identical hourly rates (s2v4m8: $0.1252 1y / $0.1157 3y).

modes.label: Planned Compute 3 years
modes.note: Planned Compute 3-year (instance-type commitment), official USD list, KR_WEST (=KR_WEST_2), Open-source OS, VAT excluded. Fixed monthly fee per committed instance type; sizes.hour = monthly/730. Early cancellation penalty = monthly fee x 50% x remaining months. Discount vs on-demand is ~35% (1y) / ~40% (3y) for standard types, not the headline 'up to 55%'. Cost Savings (hourly spend commitment) gives near-identical hourly rates (s2v4m8: $0.1252 1y / $0.1157 3y).

modes.label: Virtual Server, no contract, Windows
modes.note: Official USD list, KR_WEST, Windows column (licence included), VAT excluded.

modes.label: Accelerated Server (GPU/NPU), no contract
modes.note: Official USD list, KR_WEST, Ubuntu (open source) column, VAT excluded. 'Even when a server is stopped, the usage fee is charged the same.' RNGD is a FuriosaAI NPU.

modes.label: Accelerated Server (GPU/NPU) Spot
modes.note: Spot, no contract only; no SLA, may be reclaimed at any time.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Pay-per-use: "only charging for usage" / "Charge by used hour" (pricing page); no platform fee published. Quotas unknown, not confirmed unlimited.

caveats: On-demand rates: official USD list (KR_WEST = KR_WEST_2 'Enterprises/Finance' offering), Open-source OS column, excluding VAT (verified 2026-09-29). USD list = KRW/1150. Sovereign (KR_SOUTH) offering is KRW-only and ~20% higher; not modelled.
Billing: 'Charge by used hour'; no-contract VMs bill only while on (FAQ: no server fee when turned off, excluding GPU). Sub-hour granularity/minimum is not published; granularity left null.
Boot disk is not included: OS disk is a Block Storage volume (min 16 GB Linux) at $0.1043/GB-month SSD, billed monthly on allocation even when the VM is stopped.
Public IPv4 $0.00487/h (~$3.56/month) billed while reserved; internet egress first 20 GB/month free then $0.087/GB.
Planned Compute / Cost Savings: ~35% (1y) / ~40% (3y) off standard VMs for a fixed monthly commitment with a 50% early-cancellation penalty; headline 'up to 55%' is not typical for VMs.
Sign-up: console account + payment method; trial credit USD 260 once, valid 3 months. Default quotas not published (Quota Service, some auto-approved).

fleet.notes: Official Quota Service describes account/region resource limits and console increase requests; some auto-approve, others are not promised automatic. No public numeric fresh-account Virtual Server/vCPU/GPU limit, verification details or SLA established. Max 5 VPCs per account (FAQ); a Memory quota item was added on 2026-09-15.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Modifying Virtual Server specs, and managing creation/changes in init script and tag; Creating custom images and replicating them between accounts
snapshot_auto.note: Virtual Server 'Key Features' list covers create/manage/custom-image/replicate but names no automatic state capture on stop/sleep/timeout; only a separate scheduled Backup service (daily/weekly/monthly) exists, which is opt-in and time-scheduled, not stop-triggered. No official page states snapshot-on-stop, so 'no' stands.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Image creation: You can create an Image from the configuration of the Virtual Server you are using, and you can also create an Image by uploading your Image file to Object Storage.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk only, no memory. 'Snapshot-Based' Images of a VM can boot new Virtual Servers and be shared with other accounts (docs recommend stopping the server first for FS consistency). Block Storage volumes also have on-demand snapshots: restore in place or 'Create recovery volume' as a new volume; snapshots billed on source volume size. Console/API/CLI (API and CLI references exist).

harness_api.quote: Virtual Server allows users to assign only the amount of necessary virtual computing resources at the time when needed, without having to purchase CPU, memory or other infrastructure resources from servers.
harness_api.note: Samsung SDS Cloud Platform's Virtual Server is a plain general-purpose IaaS VM product (provisioning/storage/network/security-group console features only) with no coding-agent/harness-driving API mentioned anywhere on its product page; feature is plainly outside what this product is.

egress_allowlist.quote: When a Security Group is first created, it blocks all inbound and outbound traffic according to the default rule (Any/Deny).
egress_allowlist.note: Security Group outbound allow rules by target IP/CIDR, protocol, port; plus per-VPC Internet Gateway Firewall (also default Any Deny, IP/port/protocol rules). No FQDN rules documented.

ingress_rules.quote: Users can specify an IP address, port, and protocol to create inbound/outbound rules, and only traffic allowed by the created rules can access the target resources.
ingress_rules.note: Security Groups (default deny) plus IGW/Load Balancer firewalls; public NAT IP is opt-in.

guest_firewall.note: Full VM (Linux/Windows images) with root/Administrator via key pair; iptables/nftables/Windows Firewall work inside.

secret_proxy.quote: Remove hardcoding of sensitive information in application source code and retrieve it by calling Secrets stored securely in a Key-Value format.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets Manager / Secret Vault are KMS-encrypted secret stores the workload reads; no credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.note: Block Storage data volumes 8 GB-12 TB, SSD/HDD, online expansion; up to 26 volumes per Virtual Server.

volume_shared.quote: File Storage allows servers connected via the network to easily store and share data, making it a storage solution suitable for application environments that use multiple servers.
volume_shared.note: File Storage over NFS (Linux) or CIFS (Windows), read-write, auto-scaling capacity. Block Storage SSD/HDD_MultiAttach volumes also attach to 2+ Virtual Servers at once ('no limit on the number of servers per volume'; not for Windows).

isolation.quote: Service Architecture ... Application, Guest OS / Virtualization(Hypervisor) - CPU, Memory, Network Interface, Storage
isolation.note: Standard hypervisor-based VM isolation (Samsung SDS Cloud Platform is an OpenStack/KVM-based IaaS); exact hypervisor not publicly named, so medium confidence.

image_oci.quote: Creating custom images and replicating them between accounts
image_oci.note: not offered: Virtual Server uses whole-VM 'custom images' (disk images), not OCI/Docker images, to start machines.

docker_inside.quote: Securely connect to the OS using key pairs
docker_inside.note: derived: root SSH access to a full Linux VM means Docker can be installed and run inside it; not explicitly documented as a managed feature.

nested_virt.quote: Virtual Server allows users to assign only the amount of necessary virtual computing resources ... Virtualization(Hypervisor)
nested_virt.note: not offered: no documentation of nested virtualization/exposed /dev/kvm on standard hypervisor-based Virtual Servers.

desktop.quote: Virtual Server ... virtual computing service provides resources with optimized performance for the purpose from development to testing and running application programs in the cloud environment.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (general-purpose IaaS VM, no managed graphical desktop/VNC/RDP streaming service).

browser.quote: Virtual Server allows users to assign only the amount of necessary virtual computing resources at the time when needed
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no managed/preinstalled browser service.

computer_use.quote: Virtual Server allows users to assign only the amount of necessary virtual computing resources at the time when needed
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope, no screenshot/click driving API.

anti_bot.quote: Virtual Server allows users to assign only the amount of necessary virtual computing resources at the time when needed
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (plain IaaS VM, not a browser/agent platform).

captcha_solving.quote: Virtual Server allows users to assign only the amount of necessary virtual computing resources at the time when needed
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Basic offering : OS S/W, 100GB for OS installation disk, and 1 public IP
egress_ip_type.note: Standard hyperscaler datacenter public IPv4 per VM.

fork.quote: Creating custom images and replicating them between accounts
fork.note: Clone via custom VM image (create image, launch new VM from it), not a single-call live 'fork' API.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: derived: card's snapshot capability is disk/filesystem only ('fs'), not memory; running processes are not preserved in clones.

wake_on_request.quote: Without contract : Hourly billing for the actual usage according to the on/off status of VM
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; VM state (on/off) is user-controlled, no request-triggered auto-wake documented.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Without contract : Hourly billing for the actual usage according to the on/off status of VM
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: no idle auto-stop documented; VM billing follows manual on/off state.

live_resize.quote: the capacity of key resources such as CPU and memory can be scaled in or out while using Virtual Servers by modifying Virtual Server specifications

agent_harnesses.quote: Virtual Server allows users to assign only the amount of necessary virtual computing resources at the time when needed
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; plain IaaS VM, no coding-agent templates.

own_agent_api.quote: Virtual Server allows users to assign only the amount of necessary virtual computing resources at the time when needed
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no first-party task-agent API.

mcp_server.quote: Virtual Server allows users to assign only the amount of necessary virtual computing resources at the time when needed
mcp_server.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no MCP server for controlling sandboxes.

lang_python.quote: master OS images of various types are also offered
lang_python.note: not offered out of the box: bare OS images (Linux/Windows); users install their own runtimes, no first-party Python code-exec SDK.

lang_node.quote: master OS images of various types are also offered
lang_node.note: not offered out of the box: bare OS images; users install their own runtimes, no first-party Node code-exec SDK.

inbound_https.quote: Basic offering : OS S/W, 100GB for OS installation disk, and 1 public IP
inbound_https.note: derived: each VM gets a public IPv4 and inbound traffic control (Security Group), so users can serve HTTPS directly on the public IP; no managed per-app HTTPS URL feature.

egress_http_rules.quote: Virtual Servers are securely protected by inbound/outbound traffic control with external Internet or other VPC(Virtual Private Cloud) through Security Group service.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control is at IP/port (Security Group) level, not HTTP method/path level.

macos.quote: Offer various OS types and standard images for creating resources conveniently
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; only Linux and Windows guest OS images are offered, no macOS/Apple silicon VMs.

self_host.note: not offered: fully managed hyperscaler service; no self-hosted deployment option.

byoc.note: not offered: hyperscaler VM runs only in Samsung SDS's own cloud regions, not deployed into a customer's own cloud account.

open_source.note: Proprietary hyperscaler platform, not an open-source project.

max_session_h.quote: Without contract : Hourly billing for the actual usage according to the on/off status of VM
max_session_h.note: Standard IaaS VM runs indefinitely until the customer stops it; no maximum session duration.

arm64.quote: Various Service Types: Virtualized vCore/memory resources are provided based on the typical server specifications... Standard : Generally used computing spec(up to 16vCore, 256GB); High capacity : Provide more resources than regular specific resources
arm64.note: Card's own SKU list documents all Virtual Server generations as Intel Xeon (1st Gen Ice Lake, 2nd Gen Sapphire Rapids, 3rd Gen Granite Rapids, plus their High Capacity variants) — no ARM/Ampere/Graviton SKU is offered anywhere in the pricing data or product pages.

eu_data_residency.note: The live Virtual Server price data (loaded by the pricing page) only defines two regions, KR_WEST and KR_WEST_2, both in Korea; no EU region key exists in the pricing data or on the product pages, consistent with the card's existing regions:["asia"].

sso.note: SingleID is Samsung Cloud Platform's own IAM/access-management service, offered specifically for 'Public cloud access control for cloud operators and developers' via 'Console access control through the account assigned based on roles', and it supports SAML/OIDC federated sign-on.
